manifest.name: Gemma-4-31B-it
manifest.blurb: A 60-layer decoder with a 5:1 sliding/full attention pattern, a different head geometry and a different rope per layer type, and a sandwich of four RMSNorms per layer. Images arrive as exactly 280 pooled soft tokens scattered into the text stream.
manifest.shape_note: 60 layers · hidden 5376 · 32 Q heads · sliding layers: head_dim 256, 16 KV heads, window 1024 · full layers: head_dim 512, 4 KV heads, V = K · vocab 262144, tied · one image = 280 soft tokens.

G1_pipeline.subtitle: One decoder pass. Unlike the two video models there is no denoising loop — the loop here is autoregressive, one token at a time, over a KV cache.

notes.title: A hybrid cache, not one cache
notes.text: Five of every six layers attend only to the last 1024 positions, so their cache is bounded; the sixth keeps everything. That is what makes a 262k context affordable — only 10 of the 60 layers pay full price for it.

notes.title: This is the judge behind gemma_capfid and vid_rat
notes.text: The repo serves this checkpoint on :9001 via vLLM (TP=2) for the rationality_v5 and cap_fid evaluations. The vLLM implementation is a second tab on the nodes where the two differ — it fuses QKV and uses paged attention, so the shapes on this page are the transformers reference, not what is allocated at serving time.

notes.title: Fixed cost per image, whatever its size
notes.text: 280 soft tokens per image regardless of resolution, because the pooler divides by whatever k makes the arithmetic work. A 4× bigger image costs the language model nothing extra — it just averages harder. That is the opposite trade to Qwen3-VL, where tokens scale with pixels.

notes.title: Audio exists in the code but not in this checkpoint
notes.text: Gemma4AudioModel and a third masked_scatter branch are present in modeling_gemma4.py, but the 31B-it config has audio_config = null, so the tower is never built. Worth knowing before you go looking for an audio path that is not loaded.

notes.title: Why this is not just a cache trick
notes.text: The sliding and full layers differ in head_dim (256 vs 512), in KV head count (16 vs 4), in whether V has its own projection, and in rope. Calling them 'the same layer with a different mask' is wrong — see the attention level.

notes.title: KV sharing is implemented but off here
notes.text: num_kv_shared_layers = 0 in this checkpoint, so is_kv_shared_layer is never true and every layer computes its own K/V. The shared_kv_states plumbing still runs through every forward, carrying an empty dict.

edges.label: summed with the MLP when enabled

notes.title: The order in one line
notes.text: norm → ATTENTION → norm → add → norm → MLP → norm → add → ×layer_scalar. Four RMSNorms per layer. Wan and H3 both normalise only on the way in; Gemma brackets each sublayer on both sides.

notes.title: No conditioning signal at all
notes.text: Compare the two video models: there, six AdaLN taps per block carry the timestep and scale or gate every sublayer. A language model has nothing to condition on — the residual adds are plain, and every layer treats every token the same way.

G5_attention.title: Attention — sliding vs full, side by side
G5_attention.subtitle: One class, Gemma4TextAttention, but the layer type changes the head geometry before any token is seen. These are not the same operation with a different mask.

nodes.title: q_proj → head_dim 512
nodes.note: The full-attention layers get twice the head width. They are the ones that have to carry long-range information, and they are only 10 of 60, so the extra width is affordable.

nodes.title: k_proj only · 4 KV heads · V = K
nodes.note: On the global layers V IS K — the same tensor, no separate projection. That halves the global KV cache on top of the 4-head reduction, which is the whole point of putting the long-range layers on this geometry.

nodes.title: q_norm · k_norm · v_norm
nodes.note: A V-norm is unusual — most models normalise only Q and K. Here all three are normalised, and V's is scale-free.

nodes.title: q_norm · k_norm · v_norm
sublines: v_norm applied to K, since V = K

nodes.title: rope proportional · θ = 1 000 000
nodes.note: Big θ plus partial rotation is the long-context recipe: slow-turning frequencies on a quarter of the head, and three quarters left position-free.

nodes.title: o_proj 16384 → 5376
sublines: twice the input width, same output

notes.title: Why two geometries instead of one
notes.text: 50 cheap layers do local work on a bounded cache; 10 wide layers carry the context. Per full layer the cache holds 4 heads × 512 and V aliases K, so one global layer caches about the same bytes as one sliding layer does per token — while seeing the whole 262k window.

notes.title: What the serving path does differently
notes.text: vLLM fuses Q/K/V into one projection and selects the rope per layer type at construction, then uses paged attention with per_layer_sliding_window. Same maths, different tensors in memory — read the vllm tab when a shape on this page does not match a profile.

notes.title: How much of this file is not in this checkpoint
notes.text: modeling_gemma4.py carries an audio tower, a MoE block, KV sharing, a double-wide MLP and the Gemma-3n per-layer-input path. The 31B-it config switches all of them off. Reading the class list and assuming it describes the model is the easiest mistake to make here.

notes.title: Comparing the three models in this atlas
notes.text: Wan modulates every block by the timestep and cross-attends text. H3 puts every modality in one sequence and looks modulation up per row. Gemma has no conditioning at all — it varies the LAYERS instead, alternating two attention geometries, and brackets each sublayer in four norms.
